subject: Transient processor classification & TIA scoping for LATAM pilot
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Arias <miguel.arias@blueridgehealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Transient processor classification & TIA scoping for LATAM pilot

Hi Miguel —

Following up from our call: thanks for explaining the BlueRidge LATAM pilot architecture. Two questions to unblock the TIA scoping on our side:

1) A few of your vendor integrations (edge function that converts consent tokens) will see ephemeral request payloads for < 30 seconds and will not persist logs. For the purposes of the TIA and SCC/UK-IDTA mapping, can you confirm whether you consider those vendors "transient processors" (i.e., processing only in-memory, no persistent storage and no ability to re-identify the principal)?

2) If you do classify them as transient, do you have any supporting evidence (architecture notes, retention config screenshots) we can include in the TIA appendix? That materially changes the mitigation we propose.

Attached is a quick proposal of scoping options from our side (blueridge-tia-scope-proposal.pdf). If helpful, we can run through the suggested mapping in a 30-minute call.

Next steps: please confirm the classification and share any short evidence by next Wed (2026-05-12) so we can finalize the draft TIA.

Thanks,
Sean
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Miguel Arias <miguel.arias@blueridgehealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@blueridgehealth.com>, BlueRidge Health Legal <legal@blueridgehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 11:36:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Transient processor classification & TIA scoping for LATAM pilot

Hi Sean —

Thanks for the clear note. Short answers:

1) We believe the edge token conversion service should be a transient processor: it runs in a FaaS environment, does not write to persistent storage, and tokens are deliberately short-lived (TTL 30s).

2) I'll pull the deployment manifest and a screenshot of the function runtime config for evidence. Sophie (cc) will loop in legal if they want formal attestation.

We should be mindful of Brazil's ANPD guidance — while our service is ephemeral, local regulators sometimes treat certain transient processors differently if there is any caching in downstream analytics. We'll need the TIA text to explicitly call out no caching and no re-identification.

I can target the evidence packet by Tue 2026-05-11 EOD.

Best,
Miguel
Head of Platform Integrations
BlueRidge Health

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Transient processor classification & TIA scoping for LATAM pilot

Thanks Miguel & Sean —

If BlueRidge is comfortable classifying the edge function as transient, our TIA appendix will:
- Accept the transient processor classification as a conditional mitigation, subject to evidence that no persistent logs or downstream analytic caches are enabled.
- Require a short attestation from BlueRidge legal confirming operational controls and TTL settings.
- Add a contractual fallback: if evidence later shows persistence or re-identification capability, Redwood reserves the right to reclassify and require additional safeguards (encryption at rest, restricted subprocessor access, longer retention review).

Kimberly / Jonas — can you review the fallback language below and confirm acceptable legal phrasing for the UK addendum and SCC mapping?

Proposed fallback phrasing (draft):
"In the event that BlueRidge or its subprocessors implement persistent storage, caching, or re-identification mechanisms for data processed by the edge token conversion function, the parties agree to re-evaluate safeguards within 30 days and implement remedial controls (including but not limited to encryption at rest, limited subprocessor access, and updated technical access logs) to maintain data transfer adequacy under SCCs and/or the UK IDTA."

Naomi
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Transient processor classification & TIA scoping for LATAM pilot

Nice summary —

Legal review notes: the proposed fallback language is OK but we should be explicit about remedies tied to SCC/IDTA obligations. Suggested edits (we can insert into Naomi's draft):

1) Replace "re-evaluate safeguards within 30 days" with "notify within 7 days and remedial plan within 30 days" to ensure timely escalation.
2) Add: "Any remedial controls that materially alter processing (e.g., introduction of at-rest logging, longer retention) must be reasonably approved by Redwood where such changes affect cross-border transfer mechanisms."
3) Insert a short sentence on evidence retention: "BlueRidge will retain the attestation and evidence for audit purposes for at least 24 months and provide to Redwood upon reasonable request."

Also — attach a simple doc (transient-processor-definition-draft.docx) that defines our operational test for transient processors (stateless, TTL < 120s, no persistent logs, no KPIs derived post-processing). If BlueRidge signs to that, it will simplify acceptance.

Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Miguel Arias <miguel.arias@blueridgehealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Transient processor classification & TIA scoping for LATAM pilot

Miguel —

Thanks for the evidence packet (received Tue). BlueRidge's deployment manifest and the runtime screenshot look consistent with the transient definition, but legal requested the minor edits Kimberly proposed. We've attached the revised TIA appendix and the transient processor definition for signature.

Proposed next steps:
- BlueRidge legal to confirm the attestation and return signed transient-processor-definition by 2026-05-26.
- Redwood to finalize TIA and map to SCCs/UK-IDTA + include fallback language as edited.
- Joint 30-min walkthrough the week of 2026-05-31 to close remaining items.

If any regulators (ANPD) ask for the evidence trail, we'll provide the attachments under the TIA audit packet.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — I will coordinate the signature flow.

Sean
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
